context: Suppose n is 2 raised to a nonnegative integer power. From left to right, the columns show the remaining array length, the array of initial length n halved at each level, and one operation per level. Dark green cells and their outline mark the retained interval. Light gray cells mark the excluded interval.
description: An ellipsis at the top stands for earlier halvings. The final four levels appear below it. In the right column, downward arrows connect one light green operation square per level. The brace at the far right reads “log₂ n + 1 levels.” At the bottom, the figure also gives log₂ n + 1 as its total operation count, with an arrow to O(log n).

frames.explanation: Going from n to 1 takes log₂ n halvings. The count returned by the code with while n > 1 is exactly that number. The figure counts one more operation for the final state of length 1, so its count is one larger. For example, 8 → 4 → 2 → 1 has three halvings and four state levels. The constant difference leaves the order O(log n) unchanged. The ellipsis and four rows illustrate a general input. A small input visits only its actual levels.
frames.title: Keeping half at each step gives logarithmic growth

summary: Each round halves the remaining length. The figure pairs each retained state with one operation at that level.
